state.misconception_label: Thinks alternate angles are always equal

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are arguing about alternate angles. Tom says angles \( p \) and \( q \) are alternate. Katie says angles \( p \) and \( q \) are equal. Who is correct? ![Shows two non parallel lines that are intersected by another line. Angles P and Q are both on the outside of the lines and on opposite sides of the transversal.](). I got Only
Katie because I assumed all the angles in the figure are equal.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Actually, in this case, alternate angles are not always equal. Alternate angles are formed when a transversal intersects two lines, and they are equal only when the two lines are parallel. Since the lines in the figure are not parallel, angles \( p \) and \( q \) are not equal. Remember, alternate angles are equal only when the lines are parallel.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so Tom is correct then? Because they ARE alternate angles, but they're just not equal because the lines aren't parallel? So like, alternate angles are only equal when you have parallel lines?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: That's correct! Tom is correct in this case because angles \( p \) and \( q \) are indeed alternate angles since they are on opposite sides of the transversal. Remember, alternate angles are only equal when the lines they lie on are parallel. Great job understanding that concept!
